The Partnership acknowledges this is 'under active review' but has not yet identified how to bridge a £9.219m gap by year end.
findings.matters: A mid-year savings delivery of only 59% raises material doubt about the full-year target being met. These are not one-off technical adjustments but active programmes (workforce redesign, prescribing switches, care model changes) where slippage indicates either underestimated delivery timescales or effectiveness challenges. Failure to deliver leaves a structural deficit.
findings.figures: £13.508m of £23.923m (59%); gaps of £3.282m (prescribing), £2.218m (Individual Budgets), £1.236m (Home First), £1.107m (Locality Redesign)
findings.quote: At 30 June 2026, the Partnership has delivered £13.508m (59%) of the approved savings requirement. Delivery remains under active review through the Savings and Value Board

findings.paper_title: Financial Monitoring Report 2026/27
findings.headline: Adult social care demand is exceeding budget by £2.627m despite inflationary uplifts and planned savings.
findings.detail: Care home and care at home placements are running ahead of budget. Independent care homes have 1,422 care plans against a budgeted 1,393 (£1.236m overspend), and care at home has 2,889 plans against budgeted 2,842 (£2.218m overspend). The report attributes this to 'continued demand and cost pressures' in adult social care, reflecting both higher volumes and cost growth beyond the £23.155m inflation uplift already applied in budget setting.
findings.matters: Demand-led overspends in adult social care signal structural cost growth that cannot be solved by efficiency alone. These are real people in funded placements, not discretionary spend, and indicate either growth in elderly population requiring care or higher acuity requiring more expensive care settings.
findings.figures: 1,422 vs 1,393 care plans (independent care homes); 2,889 vs 2,842 care plans (care at home); £1.236m and £2.218m overspends respectively
findings.quote: services delegated to Social Care are projecting an overspend of £3.623m, the majority of which relates to Payments to Other Bodies, primarily Care at Home and Independent Care Home provision

findings.paper_title: Revenue Monitoring Report – Housing Revenue Account
findings.headline: RAAC remediation costs remain unquantified with funding solutions still under development
findings.detail: North Lanarkshire is managing remediation strategies for RAAC (Reinforced Autoclaved Aerated Concrete) in its housing stock. However, the potential costs and appropriate funding solutions for these works remain undetermined and will continue to be reviewed in future monitoring reports.
findings.matters: RAAC remediation can incur substantial capital costs; if funding gaps emerge, the council may need to draw reserves, reduce other programmes, or seek additional borrowing, all of which affect credit risk and service capacity.
findings.figures: No costs quantified; reserves held of £25.098m total, with £2.007m contingency (1% of budget)
findings.quote: Although significant works have been undertaken to identify and develop remediation strategies, the Service continue to consider the potential costs and appropriate funding solutions associated with the impact of Reinforced Autoclaved Aerated Concrete (RAAC). This will continue to be considered with future monitoring reports updated as appropriate.

news_drafts.headline: PPP contract obligations increasing; prior five-year saving of £4.5 million from 2023 plan is being reversed with £1 million per annum added from year 3 onwards.
news_drafts.lead: Savings being reversed mid-plan indicates planning assumptions are unreliable. Additional costs flagged as 'will be recognised in future' suggests further increases are anticipated.

news_drafts.headline: Council Tax increase limited to 7% in 2026/27 despite recommended 10%, constraining future increases; even 10% annual increase generates only £20.6m against £75.5m three-year gap.
news_drafts.lead: Council Tax is politically constrained and mathematically insufficient. The council cannot grow its way out of this gap; it must cut services or use reserves.

news_drafts.headline: Scottish Government may remove statutory capital accounting mitigations, creating uncertain but material additional revenue cost.
news_drafts.lead: This is an external policy change that could increase the effective budget gap by an unknown but material amount, or force capital programme cuts that damage service delivery.
